intent.title: Parallelize independent live cases and consolidate primitive probes

purpose: inspection evidence; not a recovery checkpoint

risks.description: Removing redundant invocations can delete distinct assertions or leave an audit disconnected from the suite owner. Require explicit assertion mapping, composed corruption negatives and current live evidence before claiming replacement; historical incomplete streams never establish acceptance.
Greater overlap can expose shared mutable state or cleanup races. Preserve accepted source and fixture lifecycle conventions; no new ownership transition or retention policy is proposed.

ownership.git_state: Maintained sources and concise approved evidence accompany the normal successful Build commit.
ownership.owner_after_creation: Repository maintainers own any new source files immediately.
ownership.owner_during_operation: Maintainers retain source ownership; executing tests read maintained inputs.
ownership.paths: Maintained live tests, test-support auditors and scheduling fixtures, and linked README documentation within the declared paths.
ownership.permitted_mutation: Reviewed source edits within this Intent; running fixtures cannot rewrite maintained sources.
ownership.upgrade_behavior: Normal reviewed Git changes update source and tests together; no migration or automatic source update.
ownership.validation: check verifies audit, selection, orchestration and corruption controls; live and independent Review establish preserved behavior.
ownership.when_exists: Inspect and amend maintained sources in place, preserving unrelated work; do not copy the broad historical Candidate.

ownership.git_state: Raw provider streams and disposable data remain ignored runtime material; concise evidence uses existing Complete publication rules.
ownership.owner_after_creation: The creating test runner owns only its new private fixture, processes and generated evidence.
ownership.owner_during_operation: Each test retains exclusive control of its mutable run state; other cases cannot mutate or clean it.
ownership.paths: Existing private live fixture repositories, writable dependency copies, child processes and per-run runtime evidence.
ownership.permitted_mutation: Mutate and remove only run-owned disposable fixtures and processes; retain diagnostic evidence under existing conventions, including failures.
ownership.upgrade_behavior: New runs create fresh state without upgrading or reusing past receipts; no new storage or retention mechanism.
ownership.validation: Offline isolation, failure propagation and cleanup controls plus live receipts verify private state and completed cleanup.
ownership.when_exists: Preserve preexisting paths and earlier evidence; use existing unique run creation and collision-safe fixture conventions.

risks.description: Fewer standalone calls and barrier-proven overlap do not guarantee lower complete cost or wall time. Include root and child provider work where available, identify cache subsets and missing usage, preserve failures, and avoid comparisons lacking equivalent workload and cache conditions.

scenarios.evidence: Actual isolated-dispatch rendezvous regression, live module-selection control, ordered-step and failure/cleanup controls, and current live case timings.
scenarios.given: Independent connected-lifecycle and Reviewer-rework cases with private fixtures and at least two ExUnit scheduling slots.
scenarios.then: The cases can overlap as separate async modules; each causal chain remains ordered, with private mutable paths, separate evidence and owned cleanup.
scenarios.when: The live selection schedules them and each performs its dependent lifecycle steps.
scenarios.wrong_result: Async annotations hide same-module serialization, steps within one lifecycle race, or fixtures share writable dependencies or evidence.

scenarios.evidence: Assertion migration table plus positive and missing/wrong-session/event/usage/schema controls; current native streams from retained lifecycle cases.
scenarios.given: Existing real lifecycle streams and the unique assertions formerly owned by the three-call primitive probe.
scenarios.then: Every former assertion has a mapped owner; successful turn completion and usage maps, exact Developer resume, distinct Reviewers, structured verdict and identity bindings remain enforced without three extra standalone calls.
scenarios.when: Retained live owners audit their own current invocations and the standalone probe is removed.
scenarios.wrong_result: A test disappears with its unique assertions, accepts a completion from another session, treats missing usage as zero, or accepts malformed or incomplete native output.

scenarios.evidence: Composed offline corruption control through the live owner's audit call and suite exit path, including incomplete completion and wrong identity; fresh live positive route.
scenarios.given: The same native receipt audit invoked by a retained live owner receives missing, incomplete, mismatched or malformed required evidence.
scenarios.then: The owning case fails and the suite reports failure, preserving owned diagnostics and settling owned work; unrelated passing evidence cannot substitute.
scenarios.when: The owner consumes the audit result.
scenarios.wrong_result: A helper detects bad output but its caller ignores it, audits stale evidence, or reports success after cleanup failure.

scenarios.evidence: Maintained before/after proof-owner map, complete current live results and lifecycle/native/profile/cold receipts; whole-suite elapsed and available cumulative provider work reported with limitations.
scenarios.given: The consolidated suite runs against the current Candidate.
scenarios.then: Public fresh Shape, continuation, approval, failed Stop correction, Build and Commit; separate Reviewer rework and exact Developer resume with fresh Review; semantic bad/good Review; native-helper routing; and cold offline validation all remain exercised with existing profile and gate constraints.
scenarios.when: The normal owners run check and live.
scenarios.wrong_result: Fewer calls are achieved by deleting a distinct proof, merging away causal controls, skipping cold validation, or reusing prior passing receipts.
